pages.title: Video editor overview
pages.description: Understand the Beam editing workspace, timeline, properties, preview, and export workflow.
pages.lead: The Video Editor turns recorded sessions and imported media into a polished composition while preserving the original source files.

sections.title: One editing workspace
paragraphs: Beam keeps project controls at the top, capability navigation and properties on the left, the output preview in the center, and timing controls in the resizable timeline below. Selecting a clip, zoom, cursor, or the canvas opens the controls that apply to it.

screenshot.caption: The canvas, properties, playback controls, and multi-track timeline remain visible together.

sections.title: From recording to export
steps: Open the editor after recording or choose an existing project.
Arrange, trim, split, and style clips on the timeline.
Set the canvas background, zooms, cursor behavior, captions, and audio.
Preview the composition at a suitable playback quality.
Export the finished video as WebM or MP4.

sections.title: Editor technology
paragraphs: The desktop interface is built with Electron and Vue. Beam uses Mediabunny for media playback and export, and the Canvas 2D API to composite visual layers.

pages.title: Video editor interface
pages.description: Learn the top bar, sidebar, canvas toolbar, timeline toolbar, tracks, selection, and playback controls.
pages.lead: The interface separates project-level actions, visual composition, item properties, and time-based editing without hiding the current output.

States are Idle, Good, Warning, and Critical.

sections.title: Sidebar and properties
paragraphs: The sidebar opens Canvas, Clip, Zooms, Cursor, Captions, Audio, and Settings. The adjacent panel changes with the active category and current selection. On narrow or short windows, labels collapse while their icons remain available.

sections.title: Timeline tracks
paragraphs: Beam creates tracks for grouped visual media, zooms, text captions, keyboard captions, system audio, microphone audio, and imported audio when those sources exist.
bullets: Click a clip to make it the current selection.
Click a track header to select every clip on that track; use Ctrl, Cmd, or Shift on track headers to build an additive track selection. The clip nearest the playhead becomes primary.
Drag visual track headers to reorder their layer order.
Move a clip or trim its start and end handles. Linked recording media move together.
Dragging media beyond the current end extends the timeline.
Click the Zoom track to add a manual zoom or the text-caption track to add an empty caption.
Right-click a clip for the supported Copy, Paste, Delete, and Hold Frame actions.

notice.title: Space has two canvas roles
notice.text: Space toggles playback, while holding Space during a drag pans a zoomed canvas. Editable fields ignore these global shortcuts.

sections.title: Direct and multiple selection
paragraphs: Click a supported visual, caption, blur layer, cursor, or screen area directly on the canvas, or select the same item on the timeline. A multiple selection uses one primary clip for the panel.
bullets: Visual appearance and transforms propagate only to compatible visual clips.
Blur properties propagate only to selected blur clips.
Volume propagates only to selected audio clips.
Caption styling propagates only to captions of the same text or keyboard subtype.
Custom caption text and Follow Cursor never propagate across a multiple selection.
Crop and canvas transformation handles require exactly one selected visual clip.

pages.title: Video editor capabilities
pages.description: Open a focused reference for every Video Editor capability and its exact settings.
pages.lead: Each capability has its own page so properties, defaults, selection rules, and edge cases remain easy to scan.
